policy: presets provide sonic capability, not musical content

presets.name: Electric Finger Bass — Modeled
strengths: pluck and pickup position shape harmonic balance without fixed unrelated resonances
frequency-dependent damping makes upper partials decay faster than the fundamental
supports deterministic pitch approaches and bass articulation attack/release scaling
limitations: single-note fingerstyle model; slap/pop, pick scrape, fret collision and continuous slide-state are outside this preset
not calibrated to a specific commercial bass or pickup measurement

presets.name: Modeled Admittance Violin
strengths: connected arco phrases across strings
modeled adjacent-string crossings
causal bridge-admittance/body feedback into string motion
limitations: physically inspired deterministic model, not a sampled concert violin or fitted named instrument
bridge admittance uses a compact modal approximation; full measured impulse-response fitting, advanced bow bounce, and continuous double stops remain outside this preset

presets.name: Modeled Articulated Violin
strengths: S12 realistic arco with S10/S11 expression and phrase control
pizzicato pluck excitation with deterministic free-string decay
harmonic touch voicing and detached spiccato bow-contact gestures
limitations: physically inspired deterministic model, not a sampled concert violin or fitted named performer
harmonic MIDI denotes sounding pitch; ricochet, sautillé, col legno, sul ponticello/tasto notation, and continuous double-stop special articulations remain outside this preset

presets.name: Modeled Continuous Violin
strengths: connected arco phrases
continuous same-string legato
modeled bow-direction changes
limitations: physically inspired deterministic model, not a sampled concert violin
continuous state currently targets monophonic same-string phrases; double-stop continuity and advanced bow bounce remain outside this preset

presets.name: Modeled Coupled Violin
strengths: connected arco phrases across strings
modeled adjacent-string crossings
residual bridge/body continuity after string changes
limitations: physically inspired deterministic model, not a sampled concert violin
coupling is a conservative bridge/body approximation; double-stop continuity, advanced bow bounce, and full body-feedback mechanics remain outside this preset

presets.name: Modeled Expression Violin
strengths: connected arco phrases across strings
deterministic performance-to-timbre microvariation without changing composition
bow attack/reversal irregularity and vibrato-coupled excitation on the S8/S9 physical model
limitations: physically inspired deterministic model, not a sampled concert violin or fitted named instrument
microvariation is a conservative control-layer model; advanced bow bounce, continuous double stops, harmonics, and pizzicato remain outside this preset

presets.name: Modeled Open Violin
strengths: sustained arco lines
bow-pressure and bow-speed response
exposed modeled-string texture
limitations: physically inspired deterministic model, not a sampled concert violin
advanced bow bounce, pizzicato, and harmonic fingering are not rendered by this preset

presets.name: Modeled Realistic Violin
strengths: connected arco phrases with S10/S11 expression control
open/stopped-string damping and vibrato behavior derived from violin realization
finite position-shift, string-crossing, and bow-retake mechanics without changing authored notes
limitations: physically inspired deterministic model, not a sampled concert violin or fitted named performer
technique hardening is conservative; harmonics, pizzicato, ricochet/spiccato bounce, and continuous double stops remain outside this preset

presets.name: Synthetic Warm Violin
strengths: sustained melody
supporting counterline
hybrid arrangements
limitations: not intended as a highly realistic exposed virtuoso solo
no pizzicato/tremolo/portamento model in this preset

presets.name: Acoustic Kit — Modeled
strengths: kick membrane modes include bounded strike-dependent tension relaxation instead of a single pitch-swept oscillator
snare combines membrane/body modes with deterministic stochastic wire collisions
closed hi-hat uses velocity-sensitive inharmonic modal decay with bounded strike variation
limitations: compact real-time approximation, not a fitted or sampled named drum kit
currently covers kick, snare and closed hi-hat; toms, ride, crash, brushes and open-hat choke state are outside this preset

presets.name: S19 Core + Ride/Crash Extension
strengths: kick, snare and closed hi-hat preserve the S19 legacy renderer exactly

ride keeps the R2/R4 decay lock while mapping authored velocity into drummer-like stick-contact authority: soft timekeeping stays plate-forward and stronger accents bring the tip transient forward without extending sustain
crash preserves delayed bloom and R4 spectral balance while authored velocity opens contact and mid/high excitation nonlinearly for stronger section accents without lengthening the tail
limitations: ride currently exposes one bow-like voice; bell articulation remains deferred
crash is a compact deterministic plate approximation, not a fitted or sampled named cymbal
open hi-hat, choke state, toms and additional percussion articulations remain outside this preservation slice

presets.name: S19 Core + Powerful Room Integration
strengths: kick, snare and closed hi-hat preserve the S19 event renderer exactly before kit-level processing
ride/crash retain the R5 performance-context source model and decay locks
shared overhead, small-room early reflections, diffuse late field and gentle parallel bus glue make authored accents excite one coherent kit space instead of isolated synthetic hits
limitations: compact deterministic recording-room approximation rather than measured microphone or room impulse responses
room/overhead integration is intentionally tuned for one close, punchy rock/pop kit perspective in this slice
ride bell, open hi-hat, choke state, toms and additional percussion articulations remain outside this slice

presets.name: S19 Core + Powerful Room + Authentic Cymbal Strike
strengths: kick, snare and closed hi-hat preserve the S19 event renderer exactly before kit-level processing
ride/crash replace noise-led contact and arbitrary modal start phase with one velocity-dependent mechanical impact event
R2/R3 short cymbal tail targets and S26 shared-kit room remain preserved
limitations: compact real-time strike approximation rather than a full FEM/BEM cymbal simulation
ride bow and crash edge/shoulder are the only cymbal gestures in S27-A
ride bell, hi-hat openness state, toms and full drummer limb validation remain later S27 slices

presets.name: S19 Core + Powerful Room + Authentic Cymbal Strike V2
strengths: kick, snare and closed hi-hat preserve the S19 event renderer exactly before kit-level processing
ride bow and crash edge use one short stick-force event followed by a dense rapidly de-phasing inharmonic plate field rather than sparse stable partials
low-order bell/gong radiation is suppressed for bow/edge strikes while R2/R3 short-tail targets and S26 shared-kit room remain preserved
limitations: compact deterministic modal-density approximation rather than a full nonlinear FEM/BEM cymbal simulation
S27-A2 currently fixes ride to bow-like and crash to edge/shoulder-like radiation; explicit strike-position authoring remains a later contract
ride bell, hi-hat openness state, toms and full drummer limb validation remain later S27 slices

presets.name: S19 Core + Dense Cymbals + Two-Plate Hi-Hat

limitations: compact event-scale collision approximation rather than a full finite-difference two-shell simulation
pedal separation is authored per articulation in S27-B; continuous within-note pedal trajectories and full limb-state validation remain later slices
legacy drum role generator still authors kick/snare/hat only unless a Composer Agent explicitly emits the new hi-hat articulation names
